comments.body:
## Spend pause engaged — 2026-09-17

The Bedrock daily spend warning is active. Recording the pause here, since this ticket owns the pause-until-next-day guidance.

**Detection.** SSM `/bedrock-spend-cap/state` now carries `warned_day: 2026-09-17`, which was not present at the previous poll this session. The `bedrock-spend-cap` Lambda's own log line confirms the live metered value has crossed the configured warning threshold and is tracking toward the hard deny threshold, with `attached=False` (the deny policy has not been applied).

**`ce_spend` is not the signal to read.** It reports `0.0` for today. Cost Explorer lags by up to 24 hours, so early in a day it reads zero regardless of actual usage. The Lambda's `metered` value is the live figure and is what drives both thresholds. Any future automation that polls this parameter must compare against `metered`, not `ce_spend` — a `ce_spend`-based guard would have failed to detect today's warning entirely. This corrects the detection approach recorded earlier in this ticket.

**Scope of the pause.** Suspended until after midnight local:

- `review_plan_start` and `verify_completion_start`
- ticket closes, because the completion gate is itself a billable LLM op
- pushes to Gerrit, because a new patchset triggers the Bedrock-backed review bot

Continuing, because none of it draws on the Bedrock account:

- tracker reads and writes
- CloudWatch and GitHub Actions monitoring
- background investigation agents already running, which execute on the harness model

**Resume condition.** After 2026-09-18 00:00 local, when the daily counter rolls over. The orchestrator loop checks the pause state on every tick and clears it automatically once that time passes.

**A confounder worth knowing before trusting the number.** The Lambda cannot price the model family that rebar's LLM operations actually use, and is falling back to a synthetic rate for all of it. That is tracked as a separate bug. The pause is being honoured regardless — a fail-closed estimate is the safe direction to be wrong in — but the accuracy of the figure that triggered it is genuinely in question.

## Context

The account runs a daily Bedrock spend cap enforced by the `bedrock-spend-cap` Lambda. It has two tiers: a **warning** tier that publishes to the `bedrock-spend-cap-alerts` SNS topic, and a **hard** tier that attaches the `BedrockDailySpendCapDeny` IAM policy to the target roles. An operator exercised the enforcement path on 2026-09-13 to validate the mechanism, so the hard tier is known to work end to end; that exercise was a deliberate test, not a real overspend.

Agents currently have no instruction covering the warning tier. When the warning fires, an agent that keeps running plan-review, code review, and completion gates drives consumption toward the hard deny. If the hard tier trips, `BedrockDailySpendCapDeny` blocks Bedrock for every target role at once, which takes out the review bot and all gate operations for the remainder of the day — a self-inflicted outage in place of a voluntary slowdown.

The cap resets on a daily boundary, so the correct response to the warning is to stop consuming and resume the following day.

## Plan

1. Add guidance to `AGENTS.md` instructing agents to stop starting new billable LLM work when the daily Bedrock spend warning is active, and to resume the next day. The guidance must state the response, not the threshold value.
2. Define "stop" precisely so it is actionable and does not strand work: finish or abandon the in-flight gate, do not start another, and record the pause on the ticket being worked so the next session can resume from a known state.
3. Document the pollable signal an agent can read to detect the condition without waiting for the SNS notification, since agent sessions are not SNS subscribers.
4. Cross-reference the existing gate-cost guidance in `AGENTS.md` so the pause rule sits with the other operating limits rather than in a new orphan section.

## Constraints

- **No cost figures, thresholds, or spend amounts in any committed file.** The `tickets` branch auto-pushes to the public GitHub mirror, and the guidance itself lives in a public repo. Refer to the threshold by name (the configured warning threshold), never by value. A prior redaction on 2026-09-12 removed tickets for exactly this reason.
- The rule must be portable: it cannot depend on a specific CI provider, and an agent with no AWS credentials must still be able to follow the written instruction.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `AGENTS.md` instructs agents to pause new billable LLM work when the daily Bedrock spend warning is active and to resume the following day.
- [ ] The guidance names the pollable detection signal and the operation that reads it.
- [ ] The guidance defines what "pause" means for in-flight versus not-yet-started gate operations, including how to record the pause so work resumes cleanly.
- [ ] No threshold value, dollar amount, or other cost figure appears in any file changed by this ticket.
- [ ] The guidance is amended into existing operating-limit guidance rather than added as a standalone section.
compiled_state.title: Pause agent work until the next day when the Bedrock daily spend warning fires
